help.howitworks.switching_service_source.backTranslation: While a download is paused: choosing another source for a file whose download had already started is accepted and saved, but nothing starts. The service and source shown remain the ones in effect and, next to the service name, a message shows where the file will go, for example Switch to Real-Debrid (rapidgator.net) on resume. A new choice replaces it; choosing the source already in use makes it disappear. After resuming, it shows Switching to … until the change has taken effect, then disappears. If a download's paused files are to go to different places, or if the destination is not known, no destination is shown. A file that never started has nothing to hand over: its new source simply applies when it starts. Choosing a service while paused works as described above, except that the download stays paused: a service that can handle the link in use takes over immediately (the badge shows it), and a service that must first prepare a copy shows Preparing … and only takes over after resuming. These messages appear on the rows of Download activity and of Downloads; both kinds can appear at the same time.

help.howitworks.backup_torrents.each_deb.backTranslation: Each debrid service has a Prepare backup torrents switch. It is on by default for AllDebrid, Debrid-Link, Premiumize and Real-Debrid, and off by default for TorBox, whose torrent limits are stricter. When it is on, that service also adds the torrents that another service is currently delivering, so as to be ready to take over if needed, and when you switch a download to another service, the torrent already started is kept as a backup instead of being removed. This uses that account's torrent slots and limits; a new download that needs a slot takes it first. Turn it off to reserve this service's slots for its own downloads: its backup torrents are then removed. A choice already saved is kept.

help.howitworks.backup_torrents.debrid_s.backTranslation: A debrid service can also add the torrents that another service is currently delivering, so as to be ready to take over if needed, and when a download switches to another service, the torrent already started can be kept as a backup instead of being removed. This is each service's Prepare backup torrents setting: on by default for AllDebrid, Debrid-Link, Premiumize and Real-Debrid, and off by default for TorBox, in that service's Additional settings, which are part of the Advanced presentation. Backup torrents use that account's torrent slots and limits; a new download that needs a slot takes it first.

help.howitworks.adding_same_thing.if_add.backTranslation: If you add a magnet, a {file_type} file, NZB or Metalink that DebridPulse is already handling (including a download that failed and was not removed), it shows Already in the queue and keeps the existing download instead of starting a second one. When two downloads turn out to fetch the same content, DebridPulse can merge them; the merged download shows Consolidated. When DebridPulse cannot prove that they match, the merged download shows Consolidated · Unverified instead. Merging does not change who requested it: each account's request remains its own.

help.howitworks.passwords_private_links..backTranslation: A username and password written in a link ({link}) are used for that download instead of being asked for, including for each file in a folder, and are removed from the link before it is saved. help.settings.users_access.user_accounts.backTranslation: User accounts lists each person with their role, their sign-in method and the enabled or disabled state of their account. Add a local account creates an account with a username and password. A role changed in Edit user applies immediately: that person's open pages reload with the new role, without signing them out. Each person has a DebridPulse username, separate from their display name: an OIDC account receives it at its first sign-in, and it is with this name that one signs in with a local password; the pencil placed next to it in the Edit user title lets you change it and keeps any saved password. Click an account's name to show its details and its activity, where a pending request can be removed individually. Disable and Remove first show the account's number of pending download requests; those requests are removed, a transfer also requested by someone else continues, and finished downloads are never touched. Disabling also ends the account's sessions and disables its tokens; removal keeps the account's history and deletes its own notification settings. A removed OIDC sign-in that comes back gets a new account, which stays disabled until you enable it. Merge combines two or more accounts into the one you choose to keep; two accounts sharing a verified email address are flagged, but only a merge combines them. DebridPulse always keeps at least one usable Admin, and you can neither change your own role nor disable your own account.
